source_level.before: Salez Problem 2.3 OPEN. NM13-01 had already proved cutoff with O(sqrt(log n)) window for line graphs of fixed-degree edge-transitive long-range expanders, a transitive spectral-expander class outside fixed-c LRE. Other current T08 work includes vanishing-LRE and large-LRE-cover quotient classes.
source_level.after: Salez Problem 2.3 remains OPEN. Added a distinct source-valid class: lexicographic products H_n=G_n[F], where G_n is any fixed-degree vertex-transitive long-range-expander sequence and F is any fixed nontrivial regular vertex-transitive graph. H_n is vertex-transitive and spectrally expanding, fails every fixed long-range-expansion constant, in fact any admissible LRE constant is polynomially small, and rate-one continuous-time SRW has cutoff.

mechanism_progress.exact_tv_sandwich: For alpha=rd/(rd+k), d_G(alpha t) <= d_H(t) <= d_G(alpha t)+(1-1/r)e^{-alpha t} for every point start.
mechanism_progress.fiber_split: The fiber-constant sector evolves exactly as the base walk sped by alpha; the fiber-orthogonal sector equals e^{-alpha t} times an internal-F heat flow and therefore dies on O(1) time.
mechanism_progress.obstruction_removed: Fixed transitive local fibers, abundant short cycles and severe failure of long-range expansion are harmless when their orthogonal sector has uniform O(1) damping. Degree inflation/tree-branching mismatch is therefore not a cutoff obstruction.
mechanism_progress.general_reduction: A proved semigroup factor/fiber criterion transfers cutoff whenever a transitive quotient carries the logarithmic-time transport and the fiber remainder has uniform exponential TV decay.
